metered_buildings.title: Metered buildings

supported_zones.title: Supported climate zones only
supported_zones.note: Our default tables only carry two climate zones, 2A and 3B. Buildings anywhere else are modelled on a blend of them, so these are the buildings the model was actually built for. We show both readings: the full sample above is the honest headline, and this narrower one is the stricter test. It is harder, not easier.
supported_zones.ci_note: No site-clustered CI is reported: the qualifying buildings come from 1 site(s) (Panther), and a bootstrap over one cluster cannot produce a real interval.

metered_buildings.question: How close is our predicted annual electricity to a real meter, and does our stated uncertainty band tell the truth?

headline.label: Interval coverage
headline.note: How often the metered total fell inside the low-to-high range we report. That range is built by varying our uncertain inputs one at a time, and 80% was the design intent; measured, it is far lower, so treat the range as input-sensitivity bounds and not as a confidence interval.

headline.label: Median absolute error
headline.note: Half of buildings are predicted closer than this, half further.

headline.label: Median signed error
headline.note: Negative means we estimate less energy than the meter recorded. The model underpredicts, and it is also widely scattered: both are true, and they need different fixes.

headline.label: Within 25%
headline.note: Share of buildings predicted within a quarter of the metered total.

headline.label: Band width
headline.note: Mean width of the low-to-high band, relative to the expected value.

metered_buildings.bins_note: Where the metered total fell relative to our low and high. Most buildings fall outside on one side or the other, which is how we know the range is too narrow; more fall above than below, which is the same low bias the median signed error shows.

weather_decomposition.note: Swapping measured station temperatures for the Open-Meteo reanalysis path. The bias is large on heating need and small on the electricity meter, because these buildings are dominated by cooling, lighting and plug loads.
weather_decomposition.caveat: Both arms use the same modelled irradiance, so this isolates temperature error only.

storey_diagnostic.note: Known limitation: all buildings are modelled as one storey scaled to total floor area. If the 4+ storey group is biased differently, that is the cause.

metered_buildings.scope: defaults-path eval: 5R1C zone model + DEF-* defaults, given area/vintage/type. Excludes geometry extraction, vision, daylight, PV (no scan or roof inputs in BDG2). Energy only; cost and CO2 not scored (state forced to CA by the contract Literal).
caveats: Truth is one annual total per building: this is a cross-sectional error distribution, not a Guideline 14 time-series fit.
Weather is site-level across only 5 sites, so the effective N for the weather-driven error term is 5, not the building count. CIs are bootstrapped over sites and are wide.
Every building is modelled as a single zone at a single storey scaled to its floor area, so a tall building's surface-to-volume ratio is wrong by construction.
Non-office uses (Education, Lodging, Entertainment, Public services, Healthcare) are run on office or residential defaults; type mismatch is inside the reported error.

The DEF default tables carry only climate zones 2A and 3B; the other four sites fall back to a blend. Each building's zone is recorded in the run record, and the supported-zone cohort is scored separately below.
Irradiance is Open-Meteo in BOTH arms (BDG2 ships none), so the arm difference isolates temperature error only, not irradiance error.

calibrated_bills.title: With a year of utility bills
calibrated_bills.question: Given one year of bills, how close is our prediction of the next year?
caveats: Calibrated on 2016 bills, tested on 2017, a year the model never saw; same 44 buildings in both columns.
Only 44 of 283 eligible buildings (16%) calibrate today; the rest are excluded, not shown at their uncalibrated values.
The 44 were already our closest (18% error without bills vs 49% across all 283), so this shows bills finishing the job on buildings we nearly fit, not a 53%-to-4% improvement.
The ranges barely improve even when the estimate does: the range problem is in how ranges are built.

provenance.method: ASHRAE Guideline 14 / IPMVP Option D, MV-04 tolerances; buildings that do not converge abstain
provenance.note: Aggregate only. The per-building output stays in the git-ignored cache at data/cache/evals/out/calibrated.json.

pv_crosscheck.title: PV yield vs PVGIS
pv_crosscheck.question: Does our modelled PV yield agree with PVGIS, an independent estimate of the same system at the same site?

pvwatts.note: developer.nrel.gov does not resolve from this environment ([Errno -5] No address associated with hostname); PVGIS is the only reference used. Matches specs/physics.md section 5.

caveats: PVGIS is a model, not a meter: agreement means two models agree, not that either is right. An empirical PV check needs metered output (e.g. the NIST campus arrays) and is not done here.
PVGIS mountingplace is recorded because free vs building moves the reference yield by 4-5%.
PV-10 compares after moving PVGIS to our plane orientation and losses; pct_diff is the raw ratio before that adjustment and will differ.

cost_check.title: Installed cost vs Tracking the Sun
cost_check.question: Is our modelled installed PV cost ordinary for this market, or are we quoting a price nobody actually pays?
cost_check.source: LBNL Tracking the Sun 2024, OEDI, partitioned by state
caveats: Tracking the Sun reports up-front price before incentives, across installers, hardware and system sizes we do not match on. Inside the IQR means our assumption is ordinary, not that a given project would cost that.
Only CA and TX are downloaded, because PropertySummary.state admits only those two.
A band built from fewer than 30 systems is flagged indicative and should not be read as a verdict.
